precepts.text: And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. This rock is Christ himself. I will build my church: the twelve tribes of Israel. precepts.point: For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty! corn shall make the young men cheerful, and new wine the maids.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “The Lord of hosts shall defend them”, and “the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: for they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land.” He is not saving all nations; he is only saving the twelve tribes. Christ says the same of his people: “And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.”

This rock is Christ himself. “I will build my church”: the church is the twelve tribes of Israel. And “the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.”

So although Britain forbade us to march, trying to hinder black excellence, hinder black unity, hinder the twelve tribes of Israel growing, Christ said the gates of hell will not prevail. They delayed the men's conference, but it still went on, and the presentations were still done. Bishops, deacons, captains, officers of thousands and officers of hundreds all know what the leadership knows, so if one is taken up there are thousands of other men who know exactly the same thing. This will not be stopped.

That is how the Lord defends them. He bends Judah as his bow, fills the bow with Ephraim, and raises up the sons of Zion against the sons of Greece, Esau, Edom, the so-called white man, making us as the sword of a mighty man. His arrow goes forth as the lightning, he goes with the whirlwinds of the south, the chariots of God, and we devour and subdue with sling stones. The church he builds on the rock cannot be stopped.

precepts.text: But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup. Read at the breaking of bread, and it is the same instruction we opened with in Lamentations 3: let us search and try our ways.
precepts.point: For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty! corn shall make the young men cheerful, and new wine the maids.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
Zechariah ends with the Lord saving “the flock of his people”, lifted up “as the stones of a crown”, filled like the bowls and the corners of the altar, drinking and making “a noise as through wine”. At the breaking of bread the class read Paul's instruction for those who drink of the Lord's cup now: “But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup.”

It is the same instruction the class opened with in Lamentations: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” Before a man eats of that bread and drinks of that cup, he has to search himself and try his ways.

So the cup of the Lord now is a call to examine ourselves and turn again to the Lord. The wine and the rejoicing of Zechariah belong to the flock he saves in that day: the twelve tribes that searched and tried their ways and turned back to him, the stones of his crown lifted up upon his land.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
“As for thee also, by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water.” What is the blood of the covenant? Hebrews answers it: “Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant.”

That is the new covenant blood of Christ. The God of peace brought Christ, the great shepherd of the sheep, back from the dead through that blood, and by the same blood he sends forth his prisoners out of the pit. We are the prisoners. The pit is the same valley as Ezekiel 37, and that pit is Babylon the Great. It has “no water”: there is no truth in this land.

So Zechariah is speaking of our deliverance by Christ's blood. The great shepherd who was brought again from the dead is the one who brings the flock out, and in the end “the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people.” All twelve tribes.

“The Lord of hosts shall defend them; and they shall devour, and subdue with sling stones”. We are going to devour all these nations, put them under our feet, break them in half. So the memorial of blowing of trumpets in Leviticus 23:24 points to the day the Lord God himself blows the trumpet, defends Israel, and lifts his people up like the stones of a crown upon his land.

So watch what Christ says: “Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin.” He took it down a level: you won't understand what I just said, but you are a servant. You are bound in your sins.

That is the prison of the prisoners of hope: bound under the nations and bound in sin. The truth, turning to the stronghold, is what makes us free.

precepts.text: Let not sin reign in your mortal body; yield your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.
precepts.point: I will render double unto thee: for your shame ye shall have double, everlasting joy, and your seed known among the Gentiles, so that all who see your children acknowledge them as the seed the Lord has blessed. Write the chain of events: awakening, tribulation, World War III, Armageddon where Christ makes his advent, deliverance, wilderness, kings and priests.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
If sin is the prison, Paul tells us how to walk out of it: “Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.” Don't let sin reign, meaning rule, within you.

“Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.”

Our bodies must be vessels of righteousness, used for the commandments of God and nothing else. That is how the prisoners of hope turn to the stronghold: no longer servants of sin, but instruments of righteousness unto God.

precepts.text: For your shame ye shall have double and everlasting joy; their seed shall be known among the Gentiles as the seed the Lord hath blessed.
precepts.point: I will render double unto thee: for your shame ye shall have double, everlasting joy, and your seed known among the Gentiles, so that all who see your children acknowledge them as the seed the Lord has blessed. Write the chain of events: awakening, tribulation, World War III, Armageddon where Christ makes his advent, deliverance, wilderness, kings and priests.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
Zechariah says “even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”. Isaiah shows what that double is: “For your shame ye shall have double”. The shame we have suffered in captivity after captivity, we shall have double for it.

“and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion”, because we are a confused people; take a look at TikTok and Instagram. “therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them.” God says “I the Lord love judgment, I hate robbery for burnt offering; and I will direct their work in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.”

Watch the double we are going to get: “And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.” We have never experienced that. Imagine walking down the street and everybody knows your kids' names and moves the hell out of their way: that's brother so-and-so's kid. All people are going to know our children. That's double.

Write down the chain of events: awakening, which is us waking up; followed by tribulation, and we are between those now; World War III; Armageddon in the midst of that war, where Christ makes his advent; deliverance; wilderness; then kings and priests, rulership.

precepts.text: When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece. Judah and Ephraim are the bow and the arrow, against the white man. That is war.
precepts.point: When I heard, my belly trembled, my lips quivered, rottenness entered my bones, that I might rest in the day of trouble. The prophets were inside the vision; they could feel the heat and smell the flesh, and Habakkuk did not want to live through it. When he cometh up unto the people he will invade them with his troops, which is why Trump created Space Force and why the UFO files are coming out: the aliens are the angels on the Lord's chariots.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
Habakkuk sees Christ coming: “Thy bow was made quite naked, according to the oaths of the tribes, even thy word.” The oaths of the tribes is the Bible. A bow in hand means you are coming for war, so according to the oaths of Jacob, Christ is coming for war. Zechariah shows what that bow is: “When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece”.

The Lord bends Judah for himself like a bow and fills the bow with Ephraim: Judah and Ephraim are the bow and the arrow. He raises up the sons of Zion, the rest of the twelve tribes, against the sons of Greece: against the Greeks, the white man. That is war.

That is why this tribulation will not be like any other we have gone through. There will be wars like we have never seen, and in the midst of world war Christ comes: Armageddon. “Thou didst march through the land in indignation, thou didst thresh the heathen in anger.” Indignation is righteous anger, and he beats the nations in it. The arrows and the glittering spear are the missiles being shot.

And the war is for his people alone: “Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, even for salvation with thine anointed”. He is only coming to save the twelve tribes of Israel. “Thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked”: that is the white man, and America is the head, discovered “unto the neck” to make sure it is finished. Judah and Ephraim in his hand are how he does it.

precepts.text: When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion.
precepts.point: When he roars, the children shall tremble from the west, and he will place them in their houses.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
“How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I deliver thee, Israel?” God is saying, how am I going to turn away from you, my son, and deliver you forever to the heathen? Admah and Zeboim were the cities round about Sodom and Gomorrah that were utterly destroyed, and he cannot do that to us. Though he strikes us with righteous judgment in these curses, he has not forgotten us. “I will not execute the fierceness of mine anger”: all the horror of these curses we deal with is mercy.

What comes after the repentance is the honor, and Zechariah shows it: “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”, that is, repent, and “even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”. Then: “When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece, and made thee as the sword of a mighty man.”

This is talking about a weapon. Judah is bent first, like the bow, and then he fills the bow with Ephraim, like an arrow. It is the same order as Hosea 11:10: he roars like a lion because the tents of Judah are raised first, and the northern kingdom sees that example and follows it, and the children tremble from the west, from the western hemisphere. Thy sons, O Greece, goes into Edom, Esau, Cain, all these countries that rule with a fist of iron.

“And the Lord shall be seen over them, and his arrow shall go forth as the lightning”. That arrow is us. Christ leads the charge, and we get to move like that too, with the two-edged sword in our hand to execute vengeance upon the heathen, the honor all his saints have. “they shall drink, and make a noise as through wine; and they shall be filled like bowls, and as the corners of the altar”: we partake in the vengeance, like the blood of the sacrifice filling the bowls thrown on the altar. We don't just stand by and watch it.

So we don't fight physically now; we repent now and fight through preaching, and God fights for us later. He will place us in our houses, tell us, you're from Asher, you're from Ephraim, from Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, Naphtali, and give us back our royal heritage and our identity.

precepts.point: The word says a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod, and Ashdod is the area of modern day Tel Aviv; this teaching places the line of Amalek dwelling there today.

note.label: Genesis 36: The Generations of Esau, Who Is Edom

precepts.why:
“And a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.”

Amalek came of Timna, a concubine to Eliphaz, a lesser wife. That is why the word bastard is studied here: in the scriptures it means a child of incest or one born outside the proper marriage. The prophecy names where that seed sits: a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod, and Ashdod is the area of modern day Tel Aviv. The line of Amalek is placed dwelling there today.

precepts.text: Thy King cometh riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass; the foal bound unto the vine is that prophecy.
precepts.point: His eyes shall be red with wine: Christ drank wine, so much that men called him a winebibber, but he was never drunken.

note.label: Genesis 49: What Shall Befall the Twelve Tribes in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.” That King is Christ, who comes from the tribe of Judah, riding into Jerusalem upon the colt.

“Binding his foal unto the vine, and his ass’s colt unto the choice vine” is that prophecy. Jacob is speaking of Shiloh, the peaceful one, Christ, the lawgiver from between Judah’s feet, unto whom the gathering of the people shall be.

precepts.text: A bastard shall dwell in Ashdod, and the pride of the Philistines shall be cut off.
precepts.point: In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“A bastard shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord; even to his tenth generation”. The children begotten of forbidden unions with the nations were shut out of the congregation. The prophets tie the bastard to a place: “And a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.”

Ashdod was one of the cities given to the tribe of Judah in the inheritance, but Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants and lost it, and there the bastard dwells. In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod; that is the bastard of Ashdod, shut out of the congregation.

precepts.text: The Most High bends Judah as His bow and fills it with Ephraim as arrows, raising up the sons of Zion against the sons of Greece, the sons of the white man.
precepts.point: He will lay His vengeance upon Edom by the hand of His people Israel, and they shall do in Edom according to His anger and His fury. This is future prophecy that has not yet come to pass, for the Most High must first change our minds to act according to His anger to perform righteous recompense with our own hands.

note.label: Ezekiel 25: Judgment on Ammon, Moab, Edom, and the Philistines

precepts.why:
“And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel”. Zechariah shows the hand: “When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece, and made thee as the sword of a mighty man.”

The Most High bends Judah as His bow and fills it with Ephraim as the arrows, and raises up the sons of Zion against the sons of Greece, the sons of the white man. Edom, the so-called white man, dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance and greatly offended, and Israel shall do in Edom “according to mine anger and according to my fury”.

This is future prophecy that has not yet come to pass. The Most High must first change our minds to act according to His anger, so that we perform righteous recompense with our own hands, as the sword of a mighty man in His hand.

precepts.point: He that remaineth, even he, shall be for our God, and he shall be as a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite. Those that remain are the ones who will reverence Israel and serve.

precepts.why:
Tyrus, Zidon, Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and the Philistines are judged for the part they had in the captivity, and they had a part. “What nation hath not had a part in her kingdom and gotten of her spoils? All her ornaments are taken away; of a free woman she is become a bondslave.”

Every nation had a part in Israel's kingdom and got of her spoils; of a free woman she became a bondslave. That is why Tyrus is cast out and devoured with fire, and the pride of the Philistines cut off.

precepts.point: He that remaineth, even he, shall be for our God, and he shall be as a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite. Those that remain are the ones who will reverence Israel and serve.

precepts.why:
“When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” The kingdom was Israel's and was lost for disobedience; the disciples knew it was to be restored again to Israel.

The nations named here spoiled that kingdom and are judged for it, and he that remaineth of them shall be for our God, as a governor in Judah and Ekron as a Jebusite: those that remain are the ones who will reverence Israel and serve when the kingdom is restored.

The oppressor is broken in pieces, and the poor of the people and the children of the needy are saved; that is why no oppressor passes through his house any more.

But ye shall be named the Priests of the Lord: men shall call you the Ministers of our God: ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles, and in their glory shall ye boast yourselves.”

The strangers feed our flocks and the sons of the alien become our plowmen and vinedressers, and we are named the Priests of the Lord and eat the riches of the Gentiles. That is the prisoners sent forth out of the pit wherein is no water.

precepts.point: Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope: even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee. We are the prisoners of hope even now.

note.label: Zechariah 9: Thy King Cometh Unto Thee, Just and Having Salvation

precepts.why:
Even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee. “For your shame ye shall have double; and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion: therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them.”

The double rendered to the prisoners of hope is for our shame: in their land they possess the double, and everlasting joy shall be unto them.

precepts.text: Thy King cometh unto thee, lowly, and riding upon an ass.
precepts.point: What he came to fulfil is the prophecies written concerning him, not the commandments given to Israel to keep. Everything in chapter 2 of this same gospel is an example of that fulfilling.

note.label: Matthew 5: The Sermon on the Mount and the Magnifying of the Law

precepts.why:
Zechariah wrote, “behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.” Christ fulfilled it when he rode into Jerusalem lowly upon an ass.

From the seed of the woman in Genesis, to the Prophet like unto Moses, the Star out of Jacob, the suffering servant of Isaiah, the pierced hands of the psalms, the Lord at the right hand, and the King on the ass, this is what was written concerning him. He came to fulfil these, not to destroy the law given to Israel to keep.

precepts.text: Tell ye the daughter of Sion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass.
precepts.point: All this was done that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet.

note.label: Matthew 21: The King Cometh Meek, and the Kingdom Taken Away

precepts.why:
Matthew says “All this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet”, and Zechariah is that prophet: “Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.”

Christ sent two disciples to fetch “an ass tied, and a colt with her”, and they set him thereon. He rode into Jerusalem lowly, on an ass and a colt, exactly as it was written, while the multitudes spread their garments and branches in the way and cried “Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord”.

The King the daughter of Zion was told to look for came to her just so, meek and sitting upon an ass. That is why the city was moved, asking “Who is this?”, and why Matthew counts it a fulfilment of the prophet.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 20

precepts.why: “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”: we are the prisoners, and our hope is to return to greatness, to who we are and always have been meant to be. “Even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”: all that we suffered. “When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim”: the southern and northern kingdoms like a weapon of war. “And raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece”: the sons of Greece are your friendly neighborhood white man. “And the Lord shall be seen over them”: that is on the other side, with the King of kings. “And subdue with sling stones.” “For they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land.”

note.label: SABBATH MORNING CLASS: Apollos Creed

precepts.why: “Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.” This goes with binding his ass’s colt unto the choice vine. Just reading it you don’t know what it is talking about; you would have to know what happened with Christ in order to know this is speaking about him.

note.label: BLACK ALLIANCE WITH A SHADOW GOVERNMENT

precepts.why:
Through God we shall do valiantly, but to do valiantly we must return to what the Bible says we are and what it says we must do. “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”: the stronghold is God’s laws, his word. “Even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”.

“When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim”: he raises Judah first and uses Judah and Ephraim like weapons of war, “and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece”. You never read that in church. We will be raised up against the white man, not today but when the Lord returns, “and made thee as the sword of a mighty man.” That is the valiantly of Psalm 60:12.

“And the Lord shall be seen over them”: that is how you know it is not right now; we are not ready. “The Lord of hosts shall defend them; and they shall devour, and subdue with sling stones; and they shall drink, and make a noise as through wine”, as if we were drunk, partying.

“And the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: for they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land.” Each man and woman like the rubies in a crown, lifted up and delivered from destruction, and all the world will see the twelve tribes of Israel. “For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty!”

note.label: ​ | Sabbath Evening Class: Secrets in the Lord's Prayer

precepts.why:
“Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”: we’re the prisoners of hope, here in America and in various other lands, always hoping for a better day, hoping for health, for safety, for longevity. The Bible says no: turn to the strong hold, and the strong hold is the Bible. “Even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”.

“When I have bent Judah for me”: Judah ain’t going to do whatever the hell they want; he’s going to bend that tribe to his will. “Filled the bow with Ephraim”: that’s the northern kingdom; Ephraim ain’t going to do what the hell they want either, he’s going to bend them too. “And raised up thy sons, O Zion”: the other tribes of Israel, “against thy sons, O Greece”: that’s against Edom. “And made thee as the sword of a mighty man”: he’s going to make us into a new sharp threshing instrument.

“And the Lord shall be seen over them”: that’s the chariots with the angels. We don’t see that right now, so in case there are any crazy brothers in here, don’t nobody go out and do nothing stupid today. “And his arrow shall go forth as the lightning”: there’s missiles and all of that. “And shall go with whirlwinds of the south”: what they call the UFOs.

“The Lord of hosts shall defend them”: God is going to defend us. “And they shall devour, and subdue with sling stones”: we’re going to devour the nations with slings and stones. “And they shall drink, and make a noise as through wine”: we’re going to make a noise like we’re drunk, laughing as we kick their butts up and down the mountains. “And they shall be filled like bowls, and as the corners of the altar.”

note.label: I Am No Longer Your Negro

precepts.why:
Judah as the bow and Ephraim as the arrow is what this speaks of: “Thou art my battle axe and weapons of war.” The Most High says that we, the nation of Israel, are his battle axe and weapons of war.

“For with thee will I break in pieces the nations, and with thee will I destroy kingdoms”: the Most High is going to use us Israelites as a threshing instrument. “And with thee will I break in pieces the horse and his rider; and with thee will I break in pieces the chariot and his rider; With thee also will I break in pieces man and woman; and with thee will I break in pieces old and young; and with thee will I break in pieces the young man and the maid.” It is going to be a hell of a time when the Most High builds us up.

That is where we are going to get to, but we have to get our minds right first. Brothers are not to do some craziness and try to start something now. The Most High is stirring many things up in the earth right now for the controversy of Zion, as Deacon Malachi brought out in his last class, but we have to get ourselves right first and be able to tell our story.

note.label: I Am No Longer Your Negro

precepts.why:
“Because that Edom hath dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and hath greatly offended, and revenged himself upon them”: that is what we have been looking at all class long, the evil of what they have done to us.

“Therefore thus saith the Lord God; I will also stretch out mine hand upon Edom”: the Most High says he is going to stretch his hand upon our enemies. “And will cut off man and beast from it”: that is the horse and the rider read in Jeremiah 51. “And I will make it desolate from Teman; and they of Dedan shall fall by the sword”: he is going to cut off their wise as well as their dumb ones, their whole nation.

“And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel.” God said he will do it, so God is going to do it. That is the battle axe and weapons of war the Most High is going to make out of the same people who are regarded as nothing. This is the same thing as raising up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece: the Most High is the one who will set it all up and change all of that.

note.label: From Desolation to Dominion

precepts.why:
“And I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow shall be cut off”: he is going to cut off wars. “And he shall speak peace unto the heathen”: we are the heathen; the Israelites are the ones called the heathen.

“And his dominion shall be from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth”: Christ’s dominion. The heathen get mad; the Palestinians have that slogan ‘from the river to the sea.’ Well, we are going to use this one: “from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth.” That is how great he shall be unto the ends of the earth.

Somebody is going to say, we’re not heathens. Oh yes we are: as long as we are African American, Puerto Rican, Haitian, those are heathen names.

note.label: From Desolation to Dominion

precepts.why: “Thus saith the Lord God; Because that Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen”. See that: the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen. Our own enemies say it of us.

note.label: From Desolation to Dominion

precepts.why:
“And that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all, that ye say, We will be as the heathen, as the families of the countries, to serve wood and stone.”

So our people in these religions, false religions, serving wood and stone, are as the heathen. That is why the Lord said he’s going to speak peace to the heathen: that’s us.

note.label: From Desolation to Dominion

precepts.why:
This goes back to the peace, speaking peace to them. “I Esdras received a charge of the Lord upon the mount Oreb, that I should go unto Israel”; go unto Israel. “But when I came unto them, they set me at nought, and despised the commandment of the Lord.”

So because of that, watch: “And therefore I say unto you, O ye heathen”. Who? O ye heathen. He’s talking to Israel. “That hear and understand, look for your Shepherd”: that’s the Shepherd in Micah 5.

“He shall give you everlasting rest”: that’s speaking peace to us, the same thing. “For he is nigh at hand, that shall come in the end of the world.” That was a heavy one.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

precepts.why: Regarding the great city, and he will smite her power in the sea: “The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.” The sea is the nations. So he will smite her power in the sea: he will smite her power among the nations. America is going to lose her power over the nations.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 2 Message to the 7 Churches

precepts.why:
Turn to the strong hold, prisoners of hope. The strong hold is the Bible. We are the prisoners of hope: America is a prison house, in case you didn’t know it. The Lord promises double, bends Judah as his bow and fills it with Ephraim, raising Zion against Greece, which is us raised up against Esau, and making his people like the sword of a mighty man.

The Lord is seen over them; his arrow goes forth as lightning, he blows the trumpet and goes with the whirlwinds of the south. He appears above his people with the angels and chariots. That is when the power to take the kingdom is given. It is not now; do not mistake the future judgment for a present command to act.

note.label: Birth of A Nation

precepts.why:
Some Christian is going to say the Bishop said bastard, he’s cussing, that’s not a man of the Lord, those Bishops and deacons are wicked. It’s in the Bible: “And a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod.”

Ashdod is in the land of Israel, right next to Ekron, right above Ashkelon. A bastard shall dwell there; that’s what it’s talking about. That’s prophetic for them people that’s there from 1948. Get mad if you want. They are not the nation born at once in Isaiah 66:8; that nation is our people.

note.label: Zechariah's Leadership

precepts.why:
The chapter before explains what that battle bow of Judah is. “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”: our brothers and sisters that were murdered, that was killed. The mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers of our people who have been murdered are hoping for a better day. Our job is to tell them to return to the stronghold: turn to the Bible and learn it the correct way. “Even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”: God says he’s going to render double unto us.

“When I have bent Judah for me”: God said, I’m going to bend the tribe of Judah. You might see a lot of things happening to Judah; there’s a reason behind it.
